kinds.name: acp_harness
kinds.doc:
Drives an Agent Client Protocol agent, and serves it as one ACP connection over a channel.

The host is the ACP client and the provider the agent: each message on the channel, either way,
is one whole JSON-RPC 2.0 message as UTF-8 JSON text. The kind never models ACP itself, so a
provider in any language implements ACP as the protocol defines it, and the version is agreed by
`initialize` on the channel.

Every method answers for the provider as configured: a host builds an instance from the
provider's settings and asks it. Every method is synchronous; a host calls them from a thread
of its own. The methods without a default are the ones a host acts on for every harness; a
default is kept only where it is a true answer for a harness that has nothing to say.

Every object a method is handed (`spawner`, `sink`) is the provider's
from then on: it destroys each, even when it refuses.

slots.name: describe
slots.doc:
Who the harness is and what its `initialize` will advertise, with nothing started: for a host
listing its harnesses. Cheap, and the same on every call.

slots.name: accounts
slots.doc:
The kinds of account the harness takes, the ways to sign in to make one, and every variable
it reads for a credential. Cheap, the same on every call, and answered as configured. The
kind [`HARNESS_LOGIN`](crate::HARNESS_LOGIN) is always listed.

slots.name: start
slots.doc:
Starts one ACP connection: messages the host sends are the client's, and the agent's come back
through `sink`. The programs it drives start through `spawner`, or the provider ignores it.

`spawner` and `sink` are handed over: the provider destroys both, even when it refuses, and
the spawner by the time it calls `closed`. It returns once the channel takes messages; the
program may start later, at `initialize` or `session/new`, and a failure then is answered in
ACP before the provider closes.

With `request.account` the provider applies the account (see
[`AccountGrant`](crate::AccountGrant)): it removes every name in its catalog's
`credential_variables` from what it starts, then sets the chosen kind's, writes the kind's
files through the spawner and starts the harness on them. With none, the environment passes
as it is and nothing is cleared.

It refuses exactly when [`refusal`](Self::refusal) would for the request's requirements and
environment, with the same status: `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` for a requirement it cannot
hold, `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for a request it cannot read (a key it does not know, a
session id that is not a UUID, a requirement's value, an account kind it does not list,
settings its schema refuses, a credential that is missing, an account id that is not 1 to
128 bytes without a control character). It refuses `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, with the
reason, an account kind it cannot apply through this spawner (one that needs a directory,
given a spawner without files). It never starts with a requirement left out.

slots.name: refusal
slots.doc:
Why the harness could not hold a connection to all of `requirements` together, started with
`environment` and running on `account`, in a sentence; `None` when it can. An empty
`environment` asks about the harness's configuration alone, and is answered. A host asks
before it starts a connection, and passes over a harness that would refuse.

`GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for requirements `start` would refuse as unreadable: a name given
twice, or a value its name does not take; and for an `account` of a kind the harness does
not list. A name the harness does not know is answered with a refusal, never `None`.

slots.name: program
slots.doc:
The program the harness starts through the spawner (a path, or a name looked up on the
`PATH` where it runs, the start's environment's `PATH` when that sets one), so a host can say
it cannot be found before it starts a connection; `None` for a harness that starts none.

slots.name: import_session
slots.doc:
Seeds a session at the host's UUID from a history, so that a later connection's
`session/resume` or `session/load` of that UUID opens it; an empty history seeds a fresh one.
The provider maps the UUID to the harness's own id and keeps the mapping. `spawner` is handed
over as `start`'s is, for a harness whose files live where its programs run.

Answers what the seed was made from and what it lost. Refuses `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`,
with the reason, when the harness cannot import at all or does not read the history's
version; `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for an id that is not a UUID or already names a session, or
a history it cannot read. Never a session left half seeded, never a silent fallback, and never
an overwrite: a host moving a session back to a harness that still holds it imports at a new
UUID or into a fresh store.

slots.name: export_session
slots.doc:
One page of the history of the session `export` names (by its UUID), in the standard
session-history format, as it is: whole lines, never more than `max_bytes`, the header on
the first page only. The pages, joined, are the export of one page as
large as the whole. `spawner` is handed over as `import_session`'s is.
Refuses `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` for a session the harness does not have,
`GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for an `after` it did not give or that the session has changed
since, and for a next line longer than `max_bytes`, as
[`LINE_TOO_LARGE`](crate::LINE_TOO_LARGE) says, `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, with the reason,
when it cannot export.

slots.name: session_record
slots.doc:
Where the harness keeps its own record of the session `query` names (by the session id it
reported, a UUID), when it keeps one and the file is there. The default, for a harness that
keeps none: none.

slots.name: prewarm
slots.doc:
Starts the programs a later connection would otherwise start itself, so that its `session/new`
finds them ready, for a harness that keeps some ahead (a warm policy of its own settings). A
connection started with this `environment`, no account and no requirements, whose session
works in `cwd`, takes what this started; `cwd` is empty for a directory the harness does not
need. The programs start through `spawner`, which is handed over as `start`'s is. It returns
once they are started or starting, and does nothing for a harness that keeps none ahead and
for settings that keep none: a host may call it for any harness. The default, for a harness
with nothing to warm: nothing.

slots.name: non_defaults
slots.doc:
Each way this configured harness departs from its defaults that its settings' schema cannot
show (the detail of a rule a setting holds as text), for the host to report beside the
differences it reads from the schema itself. The default, for settings the schema shows in
full: none.

kinds.name: channel
kinds.doc:
What the host writes on, handed back by the provider that started it.

The provider implements it and the host holds the channel object,
which may be shared between threads: `send` may be called from several
at once, each thread's messages kept in its own order. Dropping the
channel is `close(GUATIAO_OK, "")`.

slots.name: send
slots.doc:
One message to the provider, lent for the call. Returns once the
provider has taken it, which may wait on the provider; answers
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` once either side has closed, and a `send` that
was waiting when the host closed answers it too.

slots.name: close
slots.doc:
Ends the stream from the host's side, with a `guatiao_status` the
provider hands to the sink's `closed`: `GUATIAO_OK` (0) for a plain
end, an error status otherwise. `reason` is UTF-8 text for people,
lent for the call and empty when there is none: why the host gives
up. Called once, and returns without waiting for a `receive` still
running; `send` answers `GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` after it. Cannot fail,
bar a `reason` that is not UTF-8, which is refused with
`GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` before this runs and leaves the stream as
it was.

kinds.name: channel_sink
kinds.doc:
What the provider writes back on, handed in by the host.

The host implements it and hands it over with the call that starts
the channel; the provider owns it from then on, makes every call on it
from one thread at a time, and destroys it when done.

slots.name: receive
slots.doc:
One message to the host, lent for the call. Returns once the host
has taken it, and a host never waits in it for its own `send`.
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` says the host takes nothing more; any error
ends the stream, and the provider then calls `closed` with that
status and delivers nothing still queued.

slots.name: closed
slots.doc:
The stream has ended, from either side: with the host's status from
the channel's `close`, or the provider's own, a `guatiao_status`
(`GUATIAO_OK` is the normal end). `reason` is UTF-8 text for
people, lent for the call and empty when there is none: the
provider's failure, or the host's reason passed on. Called exactly
once, and nothing but `destroy` follows it. Cannot fail, bar a
`reason` that is not UTF-8, which is refused with
`GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` before this runs and leaves the stream as
it was.

kinds.name: process_spawner
kinds.doc:
Starts programs where the host chooses: on this machine, on another over SSH, in a container or
a virtual machine. The host implements it and hands one to every
[`AcpHarness::start`](crate::AcpHarness::start); the provider owns it from then on, starts its
programs through it, or never calls it, and destroys it by the time it calls the sink's
`closed`.

Every slot takes `&self`, so a provider may call it from several threads at once.

slots.name: describe
slots.doc: Where its programs run and what it can give them; the same on every call.

slots.name: spawn
slots.doc:
Starts `spec` and hands over the process. Refuses `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` a spec asking
what [`describe`](Self::describe) says it cannot give, `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` a program
that is not there, `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` a spec it cannot read.

slots.name: write_file
slots.doc:
Writes `bytes` to the file `path` in the private directory the host granted this spawner (an
account's `state_dir`, or a login's), making directories on the way and replacing a file
there; `private` makes it readable by its owner alone where the system has such a notion.

**The host resolves every path** against that directory and never trusts the provider's:
`path` is relative, and an absolute path, a `..` part, or a link leading out of the directory
is `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND`, as is any call on a spawner with no such directory. A file
with another name for the same data (a hard link) is `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` too, where the
system lets the host see it. `private` is honoured where the file is made: on Unix the file
is created owner-only (mode 0600) before it holds a byte; on Windows the granted
directory's ACL is the guard. A spawner that cannot give files says `files` false in [`describe`](Self::describe) and refuses all four
file methods `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`.

slots.name: read_file
slots.doc:
The content of the file `path`, whole. `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` for a file that is not there
or a path [`write_file`](Self::write_file) refuses; `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for one longer
than `max_bytes`, or a file that is not a regular file `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND`.

slots.name: file_info
slots.doc:
How long the file `path` is and when it last changed; `None` when it is not there.
`GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` for a path [`write_file`](Self::write_file) refuses.

slots.name: remove_file
slots.doc:
Removes the file `path`; removing a file that is not there is no error.
`GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` for a path [`write_file`](Self::write_file) refuses.

slots.name: notice
slots.doc:
Tells the host something about the connection this spawner serves that is no message of the
client's: the harness exited, gave a notice (a version it was not tested with), or a part of
the provider's own plumbing failed. The host logs it. Called from a thread of the provider's,
at any time while the connection runs, and never with client text or a value of the
environment or the credentials; a spawner that has no use for it returns `Ok`, and the
provider ignores a failure.

kinds.name: spawned_process
kinds.doc:
One program a spawner started, and everything it starts in turn.

Every slot takes `&self`, so one thread may write or kill while another waits in `read`.
Destroying it kills the whole tree, as [`kill`](Self::kill) does.

slots.name: write
slots.doc:
Writes all of `bytes` to its standard input (its terminal's, with a terminal).
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` once the input is closed or the process has ended.

slots.name: close_input
slots.doc: Closes its standard input: the program reads the end. Closing it twice is no error.

slots.name: read
slots.doc:
Copies standard output (a terminal's whole output, with one) into `dst`: the byte count;
`0` once no more can ever come; [`READ_TIMED_OUT`] after `timeout_ms` with nothing (`0`
polls); [`READ_LINK_DOWN`] while the link is down. Never skips or repeats a byte, a link
that dropped and came back included.

slots.name: read_error
slots.doc:
The same for standard error, when the spec kept it [`ErrorOutput::Separate`]; `0` at once
otherwise.

slots.name: resize
slots.doc: Resizes its terminal. `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` for a process started without one.

slots.name: wait
slots.doc: Waits up to `timeout_ms` (`0` polls) for it to end, and answers how it stands.

slots.name: kill
slots.doc:
Ends it and every process it started: its process group or job, and those that left it
when [`SpawnerInfo::kills_escaped`] says so. Killing an ended process is no error.

slots.name: link
slots.doc: Whether the link to where it runs is up, and how often it has dropped.

kinds.name: account_keeper
kinds.doc:
Where an account provider reports what happens to an account's credentials behind the host's
back. The host implements it and hands one to [`watch`](crate::AccountProvider::watch) and to
[`usage`](crate::AccountProvider::usage); the provider owns it from then on, and destroys it when
the watch stops or the call returns.

**Every live keeper of the account hears each event**, not the first to ask. An event carries a
sequence the provider counts per account; **the host deduplicates by (account, sequence)** and
orders chained rotations by it, so a keeper that hears an event twice, or two keepers of one
host that hear it once each, store it once.

A watch looks at an account's files through the spawner (every `renew_poll_ms`, 30000 by
default) and reports a changed file here. A file deleted or blanked is [`lost`](Self::lost),
never [`renewed`](Self::renewed).

slots.name: renewed
slots.doc: The harness renewed the credentials. The host stores them only when they are newer.

slots.name: lost
slots.doc:
The harness lost the login (a refused refresh blanked or deleted its file). The blank copy
is never reported as a renewal.

kinds.name: login_prompter
kinds.doc:
How a login relays its steps to the person. The host implements it, hands one to
[`login`](crate::AccountProvider::login) and renders each call; the provider owns it from then on and
destroys it when the login ends. `ask` goes sealed from the person's frontend to where the
provider runs, never through a model, a channel the agent reads or a log.

When the person cancels, every call answers `GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` and `cancelled` is true.

slots.name: say
slots.doc: Shows `text`, a line the CLI printed that the person should read.

slots.name: open_url
slots.doc: Asks the person to open a page, and to confirm a code there.

slots.name: ask
slots.doc: Asks the person to fill `form` and waits for the answer.

slots.name: cancelled
slots.doc: Whether the person cancelled the login.

kinds.name: account_provider
kinds.doc:
Owns accounts: the kinds it makes, the sign-in that makes one, the renewal and watching of its
credentials, the usage of its plan and the models it may use.

An account provider does not run an agent. A harness (`acp_harness`) applies an account the
host hands it when the account's `provides` meets what the harness accepts, and never asks how
the account was made. The host owns which accounts exist, their secrets at rest and who holds
one; the provider owns every fact about how its kinds sign in, renew, rotate and report.

Every method answers for the provider as configured: a host builds an instance from the
provider's settings and asks it. Every method is synchronous; a host calls them from a thread
of its own. Every object a method is handed (`spawner`, `prompter`, `keeper`) is the provider's
from then on, and it destroys each, even when it refuses.

A credential crosses only as a secret, and nothing a provider answers carries one: not an
answer, a refusal, an error, a log line or an argument vector.

slots.name: describe
slots.doc: Who the provider is, for a host listing its providers. Cheap, and the same on every call.

slots.name: offers
slots.doc:
The kinds of account it makes, the ways to sign in, and which kinds report usage. Cheap,
the same on every call, and answered as configured.

slots.name: provides
slots.doc:
The standards the account `account` provides: every one it can be used as, the ids a harness
matches against what it accepts. An account names only its kind and settings; this is where
they are read. A kind that lists `provides` answers that list, and a kind whose settings pick
the standards ([`PROVIDES_BY_VALUE`](crate::PROVIDES_BY_VALUE) is the usual way)
answers what the account's settings pick. The answer is the account's, not the credentials':
it reads `account.settings` and no secret, and `account.provides` is no input. Each id is a
[`standard`](crate::standard) id, none twice. May be empty for an account that cannot be
used yet.

Takes every kind the provider lists in `offers().kinds`, and, when `offers().local`, the
automatic `local` account ([`HARNESS_LOGIN`](crate::HARNESS_LOGIN)), which provides the
standard of the program itself. Any other kind is `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE`, as is an id that
is not 1 to 128 bytes without a control character. Cheap, the same on every call for the
same account, and it starts nothing.

slots.name: login
slots.doc:
Signs in to make an account of the kind the method `request.method` produces. The provider
runs the sign-in in `request.state_dir` (a program on a terminal where it needs one)
through `spawner`, reads what it prints and relays each step through `prompter`, and at the
end reads the files it wrote into the outcome's credentials. `spawner` and `prompter` are
handed over: the provider destroys both before it answers, a timeout excepted (see below).

The sign-in is one call that ends in the outcome, a refusal or a cancel. Its steps reach the
person through `prompter`: `say` and `open_url` show them what the sign-in prints, `ask`
takes back what they type or paste, and `cancelled` is how the person ends it.

When the person cancels (`prompter.cancelled()` true, or a prompter call answering
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE`), or `request.timeout_ms` passes, the provider kills the program's whole
tree and answers `GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` with `login cancelled` or `login timed out` within two
seconds. It runs a watchdog of its own: at the deadline it kills the tree and answers even
if a prompter call has not returned (the call is then left to end by itself, and the
prompter destroyed when it does), so a host's `ask` should return by `timeout_ms`. It also
checks the deadline after every prompter call and before it answers an outcome. A key the
program refused is `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` with `login refused: ` and its reason; any other
failure `GUATIAO_ERR_INTERNAL` with a reason that holds no input value and no URL query. A
method the provider does not list is `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE`; a provider with no login
method answers `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` with the reason.

slots.name: renew
slots.doc:
Renews the credentials of `request.account` with no model turn. Answers the new
credentials, or why nothing changed. `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, with the reason, for a
kind whose entry says `renews` false; `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for a kind it does not list,
an id that is not 1 to 128 bytes without a control character, or a credential that is
missing. `spawner` is handed over as `login`'s is. A refused renewal that lost the login is
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` with the reason, and the blank copy is never answered.

slots.name: watch
slots.doc:
Starts watching the account `request.account` names for a credential its program renewed or
lost behind the host's back: the files in its `state_dir`, read through `spawner`. The
watch tells `keeper` of each change, from threads of its own, and ends when the returned
object is stopped or destroyed.

A changed credential is `renewed` with the new credentials and the `revision` of the
grant it replaces; a blank or deleted one is `lost`, with a reason that holds no
credential. Each change is told once, with a `sequence` that grows with every event of the
account (renewals and losses together) and that every live watch of the same account in the
same provider instance hears, so a host deduplicates by (account, sequence) and may hand a
keeper that keeps nothing. A watch reports what it finds when it begins, so a login that is
already gone is told at once.

Refuses `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`, with the reason, a kind whose entry does not say both
`rotates` and `state_dir`, or a spawner without files; `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for a kind
it does not list, an id that is not 1 to 128 bytes without a control character, or a
credential that is missing. `spawner` and `keeper` are handed over to the watch: it
destroys both when it is stopped, and at once when it refuses.

slots.name: usage
slots.doc:
What the plan behind `query.account` has used and has left, with no session and no model
turn: the account's windows, how much of each is used, when each resets and which models it
covers. Cheap, so a host may poll it as often as it likes. A kind the provider lists in
`offers().usage` answers `supported`; any other kind it lists answers "not offered",
[`AccountUsage::unsupported`], which is a true answer. The automatic `local` account (kind
[`HARNESS_LOGIN`](crate::HARNESS_LOGIN), when `offers().local`) is asked of the program on
the configuration as it stands. A kind it neither lists nor offers as `local` is
`GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE`, as is an id that is not 1 to 128 bytes without a control
character.

**Plan usage only.** The tokens a session or a run spent are not an account's: ACP reports
them with the session, and no field of the answer holds one. Never carries a value of the
environment or the credentials. A provider that runs a program to ask runs it through
`spawner`, on the account's directory, and destroys it; `keeper` is handed over as
`watch`'s is, for a login the call sees renewed or lost, and is destroyed before the call
answers.

slots.name: models
slots.doc:
The models the account behind `query.account` may use, with no model turn and no session:
what a host shows a person choosing one before a session starts. The listing is the
account's, so an account of another kind (another login, another key) may list others. A
provider that cannot list for a kind (the program lists its models only in a session, or
has no way to) answers [`ModelListing::unknown`] with the reason, which is a true answer,
and one that tried and could not answers [`ModelListing::unavailable`]; it never guesses.

Takes every kind the provider lists in `offers().kinds`, and [`HARNESS_LOGIN`](crate::HARNESS_LOGIN)
(the automatic `local` account) when `offers().local`: the program asked as its
configuration stands, with nothing applied. Any other kind is `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE`, as
is an id that is not 1 to 128 bytes without a control character. Never carries a value of
the environment or the credentials.

A provider that runs a program to ask runs it through `spawner`, on the account's directory,
and destroys it; `keeper` is handed over as `watch`'s is, for a login the call sees renewed
or lost, and is destroyed before the call answers.

slots.name: signed_in
slots.doc:
Whether the program's own login (the automatic `local` account) exists, asked cheaply enough
for a host to list the account only when it does, with no list of file names of its own.

The answer is [`SignedInState::SignedIn`] when a login is there, [`SignedInState::SignedOut`]
when every place the program keeps one was looked at and none holds one, and
[`SignedInState::Unknown`] when the provider could not tell (a place it cannot look at here,
a keyring that did not answer in time), each of the last two with a reason. A login counts
where the program finds one: a credentials file that is not empty, an entry of the
operating system's keyring or keychain, or one of the variables the program signs in by
itself with, set and not empty (`variable` names it).

It starts no program, makes no network call, puts no secret in the answer and is bounded in
time: a keyring that is slow answers unknown instead of waiting. A login that is there is
not checked with the service, so an expired one still answers signed in. It reads this
machine's own files and keyring, which are the program's when the host runs it here. Never
carries a value of the environment or of the login, not in the answer, not in an error.

A provider that does not offer the automatic `local` account answers
`GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` with the reason.

kinds.name: account_watch
kinds.doc:
A watch of one account, from [`AccountProvider::watch`]. Destroying it stops it, as
[`stop`](Self::stop) does.

slots.name: stop
slots.doc:
Ends the watch: no keeper call starts after it answers, one under way has finished, and the
spawner and the keeper it was handed are destroyed. Stopping it twice is no error.
